What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.

KTPH000Four new AI diagram typesKTPH001 — besides the logical-structure flowchart, the snippet editor can now generate KTPH002sequenceKTPH003, KTPH004stateKTPH005, KTPH006classKTPH007, and KTPH008ERKTPH009 diagrams. Each family uses its own compact, safety-restricted Mermaid dialect and its own built-in quality skill, and renders in the bundled offline Mermaid renderer as before. See KTPH010Mermaid diagramsKTPH011.

KTPH000Several diagrams per snippetKTPH001 — a snippet now stores any number of diagrams. The diagram window lists them with family, title, and line range, offers KTPH002New diagramKTPH003 with a type choice, and can KTPH004DeleteKTPH005 a selected diagram; KTPH006RegenerateKTPH007 keeps each diagram's family and scope.

KTPH000Diagram from a selectionKTPH001 — select part of a script and pick a diagram type from the editor's new KTPH002Generate diagramKTPH003 context submenu to diagram just those lines. The diagram remembers the line range, its code references point at the real snippet lines, and regeneration re-reads the same lines.

KTPH000Diagrams no longer fail on thinking modelsKTPH001 — the diagram request's output budget covered the model's hidden reasoning as well, so a reasoning model could use up the whole budget before writing a single character of the diagram, and generation failed after minutes of work. The budget now leaves room for that reasoning, and a response that is still cut off says so instead of reporting a generic failure.

KTPH000AI code actions no longer translate your script's commentsKTPH001 — every action that rewrites code used to force the snippet's comments, messages, log lines and help text into the configured KTPH002Text languageKTPH003, which defaults to korTTY's own interface language. Running korTTY in German and applying a KTPH004Full code analysisKTPH005 result to an English script therefore translated the whole file's prose, without asking. korTTY now keeps the language the script is already written in and only writes new text to match. Translating is still available — select a language under KTPH006Text languageKTPH007 — but it is now something you ask for. Where korTTY cannot tell which language a script uses, because there is too little text or the comments mix languages, it asks once per snippet instead of guessing. This applies to Full code analysis, security fixes, the improve and assist actions, alternatives, one-liners and code completion.

KTPH000The KTPH001Full code analysisKTPH002 review preview no longer freezes korTTYKTPH003 — while the preview of a finished run was open, no terminal session accepted input and the processing window beside it could not even be scrolled, because the preview blocked the whole application. It no longer does: your sessions keep running and you can read what the run did while you review its result. Since the snippet can now be edited during the review, korTTY checks before applying that the editor still holds the text the result came from, and refuses rather than overwriting newer edits.

KTPH000The analysis, processing and preview windows now dock into one surfaceKTPH001 — the review preview attaches to the free side of the KTPH002Full code analysisKTPH003 window and the AI-processing window to the other, both matching its height and following it as it moves. korTTY makes room by sliding the analysis window, and narrows it only when all three cannot fit side by side. Each docked window can be resized and its width is remembered; dragging one away detaches it, and KTPH004Arrange windowsKTPH005 lays all three out again.

KTPH000The processing window now stays open with a run summaryKTPH001 — it used to disappear together with the preview, taking the numbers with it. It now remains, reporting the run's duration, the prompt/completion/total token usage, the AI profile used, how many work items completed and how many repair attempts were needed, with KTPH002Copy summaryKTPH003 and KTPH004Show preview againKTPH005. Closing the analysis window clears the group.

KTPH000New category icons in the analysis reportKTPH001 — Security, Optimization, Design and Dependencies are marked by a padlock, a gauge, stacked layers and a module hexagon. The previous set was hard to read at a glance; "Design" in particular was a water drop, which said nothing about code structure. The same icons are used in the report, the processing checklist, the review preview's explanation cards and the exported HTML and PDF.

KTPH000KTPH001Full code analysisKTPH002 no longer fails on some local reasoning modelsKTPH003 — when korTTY requests a strictly structured result from a local server, certain reasoning models return their complete answer in the reasoning channel and leave the actual reply empty. korTTY treated this as an empty reply and discarded a finished analysis after minutes of work. korTTY now detects such a reply and uses the analysis it already contains. Only if that text is unusable does it ask a second time, without the strict format. This was observed with the newer Qwen reasoning models in LM Studio, and it affected KTPH004Full code analysisKTPH005 and KTPH006Apply selectedKTPH007 in the snippet editor. Models that return a normal reply are unaffected.

KTPH002Open in Snippet Editor no longer resolves the wrong path after a user switchKTPH003 — after switching identity inside a session, with KTPH000 for example, or an KTPH001 typed into a local shell, the context-menu entry resolved a selected file name against the original login's directories and loaded nothing, or a wrong same-named file. The entry is now greyed out while the session runs as a different identity and re-enables on its own once the prompt shows the original user again. See KTPH004Local shell tabsKTPH005.

KTPH000A split no longer asks again for the reason of the connectionKTPH001 — when a server wants a reason for the operation, as a CyberArk-style jump host does, every split of a tab opened that dialog again although the reason had been given when the tab was opened. korTTY now sends the answer already given in that tab. It is still sent rather than skipped, because a server that asks for a reason closes a session that answers with nothing. A split to a different server, or a server asking something else, is asked once as well, and a new tab always starts by asking. If the server refuses the reason, because a ticket number has expired in the meantime for example, korTTY drops it and asks again. See KTPH002Split-screen with broadcastKTPH003.

Only the current release is listed here, so the guide stays short in every language it is translated into. Every version is on the KTPH002GitHub releases pageKTPH003; the curated notes for earlier versions are kept in the repository, in KTPH000 and KTPH001.
